summary: On 19 July 2022 multiple redundant cooling systems in one London data center failed during a record heat wave. Google powered it down to protect hardware and services in europe-west2 were disrupted for many hours.

overview.background: Zone europe-west2-a in London ran in a data center whose cooling could not keep it at a safe temperature. A legacy placement algorithm let one data center issue affect three storage clusters.
systems: Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Bigtable, BigQuery
GKE, Memorystore, Filestore and many more
overview.impact: Google lists 18 hours 23 minutes of total cloud service impact and a long tail to 21:20 on 20 July. About 35 percent of VMs in zone a were terminated and about 38 percent of Persistent Disk volumes in zone a were unavailable.
overview.severity: A regional event. Google called the quality level not what it strives for.
overview.gaps: The page's engineer-engagement time differs between reports (06:40 and 07:02).

archNote: Components and relationships come from the cited source where it describes them. Layout and labels are ours.

diagrams.title: Cooling fails, services fail across layers
diagrams.caption: Temperature rose, Google powered services down, and a routing change plus an old placement algorithm let the failure reach beyond one zone.

nodes.label: Data center powered down to protect hardware
Zone a: VMs, disks, SQL, Bigtable, GKE
Region: traffic routing change, Cloud Storage clusters

diagrams.title: Thermal failover and load reduction (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: Google planned to repair failover automation, reduce thermal load progressively and audit cooling worldwide. This picture shows the idea.

afterChanges: Load is reduced step by step instead of powering off the whole room.
A zone failure stays in its zone.
Customers can move to other zones.
afterNote: The after picture shows the corrective ideas in the source and general good practice. It is conceptual unless the source says otherwise.
timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: Cooling impairment begins per the preliminary report.
Automated monitoring alerts engineers to two cooling systems.
Compute Engine terminates 42 percent of preemptible VMs in the region.
About 38 percent of Persistent Disk volumes in zone a are unavailable.
The impacted data center is powered down and its VMs are terminated.
The cooling system is repaired and restoration begins.
A majority of Compute Engine VMs are back online.
The incident is fully mitigated and closed.

rootCause.trigger: Extreme outside temperature combined with a simultaneous failure of multiple redundant cooling systems.
rootCause.underlying: The data center could not stay at a safe temperature and had to be powered down.
contributing: Failover automation did not work as intended
Traffic routing was changed to avoid all three zones, not just zone a
A legacy placement algorithm let one data center affect three storage clusters

evidence.label: The cause
evidence.body: a simultaneous failure of multiple, redundant cooling systems in one of the data centers

evidence.label: The acknowledgement
evidence.body: This is not the level of quality and reliability we strive to offer you

evidence.label: A simulated temperature alert
evidence.body:
alert: RoomTemperatureHigh
expr: avg(room_temp_c) > 32
for: 5m
actions: [page-facilities, begin-load-shed]
evidence.note: Shows a rule that starts progressive load reduction. Invented values.

diagnose.step: Check temperature sensors and cooling unit status.
Map which zones and storage clusters share the data center.

diagnose.why: A routing change hit all zones.

correct.step: Shed load progressively and power down in a controlled order.
Restore cooling then bring services up in steps.

verify.step: Check disks, VMs and databases for consistency.
verify.why: About 96 percent of disks recovered automatically and the rest later.

prevent.step: Repair and test zonal failover automation.

fix.safety: Powering down servers early protects hardware but causes an outage. Practise the order so recovery is quick and data is safe.

troubleshoot.scenario: Room temperature is rising and two cooling units are down on the hottest day of the year. Services in the zone are slowing.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do and in what order?
troubleshoot.answer: Reduce load progressively, shed non-critical workloads, fail over what you can to other zones, power down in order if needed, repair cooling, then restore in stages.

remediation.answer: Thresholds, who is paged, which load goes first, and when to power down.
No more than one storage cluster per data center for a region replica set.

design.prompt: Design a regional service that survives the loss of one data center in heat.
design.answer: Spread replicas across data centers, test failover, set thermal thresholds, and keep capacity in other zones.

checks.q: What share of zone a VMs were terminated?

checks.why: Three storage clusters were affected by one data center.
